title: A width you type into a text box has a floor, like the one you drag
goal: Typing a very small number into a text box's W field, say 1 or 12, leaves an unreadable sliver of a column many lines tall. Dragging the same edge on the canvas will not go below about 80 points. The typed field should stop at the same place the drag does, so both ways of setting a width agree.
notes: LayerGeometry.clampedSide floors at minimumSide = 1 for every layer; CanvasView.resizedFrame floors a text drag at TextRasterizer.minimumTextWidth (80). Either LayerGeometry needs a per-layer floor or LayerGeometrySelection.applying needs to ask the layer. Found while building a-label-grows-to-fit-what-it-says.
acceptance: Typing a width below the canvas minimum into W lands on the minimum instead
The number the field shows afterwards is the number the box actually took
Dragging the same edge and typing the same number end at the same width

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Only text has a drag floor above 1 (Handles.resize floors every other layer at 1, the same number LayerGeometry.clampedSide uses), so the disagreement is text-only and the fix is a per-layer floor, not a new global minimum. Two things the task did not say but a person would hit: (1) the down arrow in the W field shows the number it asked for even when the layer refused it, so a text box at 80 reads 79 while it is still 80; (2) typing 12 and watching it become 80 with no word anywhere reads as a broken field, so the W hover tip should say where it stops. Both are in scope of 'the number the field shows is the number the box took'. Shortest version: one floor constant in core, LayerGeometryEditing carries it per layer, the field displays what landed.

Built. One floor number in core (TextMeasurement.minimumWidth = 80; TextRasterizer.minimumTextWidth is now that constant, so the canvas drag and the typed field cannot drift apart). LayerGeometryEditing carries minimumWidth/minimumHeight per layer and answers minimum(for:); LayerGeometry.applying takes notBelow:; LayerGeometrySelection passes each member's own floor, so one number can land at 12 on a rectangle and 80 on a label in the same selection. Added LayerGeometrySelection.landing(_:in:) so the field shows what the layers took rather than what was typed, which also stops the down arrow counting 79 on a box still at 80. The W hover tip now says where it stops.

Verified in the probe app, not just in tests: Scripts/playtest/text-width-floor-walk.json places a label 132 wide, drags its right edge as far left as it goes (stops at 80), undoes, types 12 into W (lands at 80, height re-wraps 21 -> 38), and the focus lines report the W field holding "80" after the type and again after a down arrow. 2767 tests green. Screenshot 2026-09-04-typed-width-floor-1.png is a real screen capture (probe holds Screen Recording).

Post-build review. The hover tip is the one piece not photographed: the playtest hover step only finds toolbar tooltips, so the copy is covered by a core test instead. Left alone deliberately: whether 80 is the right floor at all is a product question, and it is asked in the audit rather than changed here.

A typed width now stops where the dragged one does: text floors at 80 both ways (one constant, TextMeasurement.minimumWidth, read per layer through LayerGeometryEditing.minimum(for:)), the W field shows what the box took rather than what was typed, and an arrow key holds at the floor. Verified in the probe with Scripts/playtest/text-width-floor-walk.json plus 2767 green tests; audit queue/audits/2026-09-04-typed-width-floor.json with a real screen capture.
